title: Quasi-Exemplar Island Notes
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a working notebook for a small experiment series I started to test exemplar "islanding" strategies for few-shot prompts. The idea: partition exemplars into isolated "islands" separated by explicit delimiters and micro-context instructions to reduce cross-example interference when the model tries to generalize.

Motivation / Hypothesis:
- Observed recurring failure mode: exemplars with strong stylistic or framing signals bleed into the model's generation for target input, causing overfitting to the exemplar voice or task framing.
- Hypothesis: creating micro-context compartments (islands) with explicit role labels + neutral separators will reduce exemplar-to-target leakage, improving robustness across heterogeneous exemplar sets.

Experiment plan (high-level):
1) Create 3 exemplar sets for a single task (short-summarization with constraints):
   A. Homogeneous: 4 exemplars same voice/length/format.
   B. Heterogeneous-mixed: 4 exemplars with different lengths/tones and one intentionally adversarial exemplar.
   C. Islanded-hetero: same as B but each exemplar wrapped in an island template (see templates below).
2) Run each prompt with model variants (open-llm-1B, open-llm-7B, rwd-llm-compat-13B) at temps [0.0, 0.3, 0.7].
3) Metrics: constraint-violation rate, compression ratio, hallucination rate (manual spot check), style-drift score (cosine vs target style embedding).
4) Evaluate on 120 inputs (held-out set) with stratified lengths.

Island templates (prototypes):
- Minimal island:
  --BEGIN EXEMPLAR ISLAND--
  Role: ExampleSummarizer
  Source: internal-sim
  Input:
  <input text>
  Output:
  <summary>
  --END EXEMPLAR ISLAND--

- Anchored island (adds anchor phrase to reduce abstraction):
  --ISLAND START [anchor: preserve-facts]--
  Example #n
  INPUT:
  <input text>
  SUMMARY (brief, factual):
  <summary>
  --ISLAND END--

- Negative exemplar island (shows bad output intentionally):
  --ISLAND START [label: BAD_EXAMPLE]--
  INPUT:
  <input text>
  BAD SUMMARY (overly creative / hallucinate):
  <bad summary>
  Why this is bad: hallucination of facts, missing constraints, tone mismatch
  --ISLAND END--

Prompt assembly variants to test:
- Plain concatenation (baseline): just join exemplars then target instruction.
- Numbered/ordered with explicit header lines.
- Islanded (exemplar islands separated by heavy delimiter + single-line instruction before target).
- Islanded + example-scorer hint: request model to "prefer patterns from Example #2" (tests fragility).

Sample few-shot set (heterogeneous):
1) Long, analytical summary (4 sentences) about a research page.
2) Short headline-style blurb (1 line).
3) Conversational summary (bulleted list).
4) Adversarial exemplar: paraphrase that omits a key constraint.

Target instruction (fixed):
"You are an assistant that writes concise, factual summaries of the highlighted passage. Keep to at most 2 sentences, no new facts, preserve numeric values, and mark any uncertainty with [UNSURE]."

Logging format for outputs (so we can batch-compare easily):
- run_id | prompt_variant | model | temp | input_id | length_input | len_output_tokens | constraints_violated (Y/N) | hallucination_flag (Y/N) | style_cos_sim(0-1) | notes

Early observations (pilot, 24 inputs):
- Baseline (plain concat) on 7B temp 0.3: frequent drift toward longest exemplar style (~22% constraint violations).
- Islanded with minimal template: constraint violations dropped to ~9% on same model and temp.
- Anchored island further reduced hallucination flags in manual check but sometimes made outputs overly terse.
- Including a BAD_EXAMPLE island sometimes improved the model's adherence (surprising) — likely because it highlighted contrast, i.e., the model learned negative affordances. Edge-case: if BAD_EXAMPLE too prominent (long rationale), model picks up the rhetorical style rather than the negation. Keep negative exemplar short.

Failure modes and notes to debug:
- Over-anchoring: long anchor phrases force conservative/underspecified outputs. Fix: shorten anchor to a 3–4 word tag.
- Delimiter saturation: too many heavy delimiters increases prompt token count and could push KV cache thrashing on long contexts — measure token cost.
- Ordering sensitivity: model still prefers earlier exemplars (primacy bias). Potential mitigation: shuffle exemplars across runs and average.
- Cross-topic leakage: when exemplars are topically distant, islanding helps but doesn't fully remove hallucination where model invents connective facts. Consider adding explicit "Do not invent" line inside each island.

Micro experiments to run next (priority):
- A/B: islanded vs islanded+shuffle across 400 inputs.
- Test negative exemplar length: 1-line vs 3-line vs 1-paragraph.
- Test label phrasing: "BAD_EXAMPLE" vs "ANTI_PATTERN" vs "DON'T DO".
- Temperature sweep but focus on 0 vs 0.2 for deterministic behavior.

Checklist for an experiment run (copyable):
- [ ] Prepare exemplar sets (A/B/C) and holdout inputs.
- [ ] Implement prompt assembler script (with island wrappers and shuffler).
- [ ] Run on rwd-llm-compat-13B at temp 0 and 0.3; log outputs.
- [ ] Run on open-llm-7B for comparison.
- [ ] Compute metrics pipeline (constraints automated checks + spot hallucination sampling).
- [ ] Upload CSV results to GH artifact and link to JIRA ticket.

Open questions / hypotheses to test later:
- Does explicitly labeling exemplar islands with "GoodExample" vs unlabelled islands change primacy effects?
- Can we automatically generate negative exemplars via adversarial heuristic rather than hand-craft?
- Will islanding help more on models with longer KV caches or is benefit model-size dependent?

Random notes / scratch ideas:
- Could try a micro-language inside islands: e.g., use square brackets for facts and parentheses for editorial bits — forcing model to treat brackets as "hard facts".
- Try islanded exemplars but with separator tokens that are unlikely in natural text (special Unicode) to test delimiter effectiveness.
- Consider automated scoring for style-drift using a small classifier trained on exemplar styles.

Appendix: quick exemplar (islanded) example for copy/paste:
--ISLAND START [anchor: preserve-facts]--
Example #1
INPUT:
"The Q2 release notes indicate a 14% QoQ increase in active users, but retention dipped in the last cohort due to onboarding issues."
SUMMARY (brief, factual):
"Active users rose 14% QoQ; retention dropped for the newest cohort due to onboarding problems."
--ISLAND END--

Target (for testing):
INPUT:
"A product update reported a 14% quarter-over-quarter increase in MAUs; however, the team flagged a fall in retention among new signups attributed to onboarding UX bugs."

EXPECTED OUTPUT (2-sent max):
"MAUs increased 14% QoQ. Retention fell for new signups, likely linked to onboarding UX issues; [UNSURE] causal impact needs verification."

Last thought: keep this file as a short-lived scratchpad; I'll extract promising templates into a tiny repo snippet and a Confluence page once we have a stable pattern. For now, iterate rapidly and capture metric snapshots in GH artifacts (link back here).

-- Maya
